label: Fantasy
title: Shadows over the Amber Court
premise: At the Amber Court, a palace of golden stone where runes burn in the walls, the eve of the solstice is being celebrated with embassies from the forest and the fey court. That night the regent does not live to see the dawn, and the doors, sealed by magic, shut in five people he trusted.

victim.name: Aurel of Amber
victim.description: He had ruled the Amber Court since the old king's death, on behalf of an heir who was still a child. Shrewd, suspicious and generous only to those he found useful, he kept half the court's secrets in his correspondence and knew how to use them.

She speaks slowly and formally, in short sentences, with a calm that can pass for coldness. She reaches for images from nature (roots, branches, tracks, wind) to explain herself, and would rather keep silent than speak of anything she has not seen with her own eyes.

motives: Had forged the old king's will to seize crown lands. {victim} had discovered the false seal and meant to lay it before the council the next day.
Had sold the lords of the north the pattern of the runes that guard the walls. {victim} held the letter that proved it and meant to order an arrest the next day.
Had stolen the sacred amber stones from the treasury and sold them to smugglers. {victim} had ordered the treasury recounted and meant to denounce the theft the next day.
Had secretly sworn fealty to the Queen of the Forest against the crown. {victim} had learnt of it from a spy and meant to decree banishment the next day.
Had slowly poisoned the old chancellor to take the chancellor's place at court. {victim} had gathered the servants' testimony and meant to sit in judgement the next day.

arrivals: You cross the drawbridge as the last solstice bell dies away. The walls of golden stone still hold the warmth of the day, and the runes on the great gates kindle as you pass, one by one, as though they knew you.

A page with a torch awaits you in the courtyard and says not a word. He leads you through corridors where the amber in the walls catches the light like honey, while far off plays a fey music no one has dared to interrupt.

You arrive on horseback under a fine rain that smells of resin. The sentries lower their spears at the sight of the royal seal on your letter, and the palace gates close behind you with a rumble of stone on stone.

Your carriage halts at the foot of the palace steps, where the festival garlands still hang. Inside, the tables are still laid and the candles lit, as if the whole court had frozen in the middle of a toast.
tensions: The runes have sealed the palace gates until dawn: no one comes in and no one goes out. Whoever did it is still here, within these golden walls.
Rumours are already running through the corridors, and each one points at someone different. You have until the dawn light touches the throne to sift the truth from the poison of wagging tongues.
Five people wait in separate rooms, and every one of them had something to lose. The whole palace is holding its breath.

night: The fey music in the banqueting hall falls silent at last, and the palace is left alone with the crackle of the braziers and the wind at the windows.
A fine rain begins to fall, smelling of resin. On the great gates, the runes of the seal burn steady: no one will leave before dawn.
The banquet candles burn down on the laid tables. A servant goes by snuffing them one by one, not daring to raise his eyes.
The wind rises and sets the tower shutters banging. In the corridors, the servants' whispers break off sharply as you pass.
Thunder rolls over the royal forest. The runes in the walls flicker for an instant, and it seems no one in the whole palace breathes.
The storm lashes the walls in full fury, and the throne braziers all but die. The night seems endless, and someone within these walls is counting every moment.
epilogues: You gather the court beneath the vault of the throne room as the runes begin to pale. When you speak the name of {culprit}, no one says a word; only the chamberlain steps forward and strikes the flagstones with the staff of office. {culprit} offers no resistance and follows the guard down the corridor; the echo of their footsteps is slow to fade. At dawn the seal on the gates melts away like frost, and the first light of the solstice touches the amber throne.

The chamberlain hears your reasoning without interrupting, the watch ledger clutched to his chest. When you finish, he closes his eyes for a moment and orders the guard to find {culprit}. They come upon {culprit} by a tall window, watching the rain, with trembling hands as the shackles close. No one enters {scene} again that night. With the first light the storm withdraws towards the forest, and the runes on the gates go out one by one, as if the palace were at last letting out its breath.

You lay out what the night has taught you before the five people the magic shut in. When you finish, every gaze turns to {culprit} at once, like leaves turned by the wind. The chamberlain strikes the floor with his staff and the guard surrounds {culprit}, who neither begs for mercy nor looks away. Outside, the sky pales above the walls. When the dawn light reaches the throne, the whole court knows that the death of {victim} will not go unanswered.
